content:
morgan: heads up — canary shows a streaming latency regression after the api-protocol merge earlier today. p99 for first token jumped a lot. :grimacing:
deploy-bot: deployed canary sha abcdef1 to canary at 2026-03-17T20:33:09Z
ajaz: saw the alert too, reproducing locally. tool-calling flows especially. first SSE event delayed ~150-250ms compared to baseline. :eyes:
liam: quick numbers from our synthetic chat workload: p50 45ms -> 60ms, p95 120ms -> 340ms, p99 220ms -> 820ms (first token). throughput unaffected, just initial latency.
sana: is there a recent PR that touched streaming/serialization?
morgan: suspect PR #2345 (rework/protocol: unify frame serialization). it introduced a small buffer/flush change and consolidated JSON framing.
arjun: starting a bisect now to be sure. if it's the protocol change we can revert quickly.
jaz: while bisect runs, I captured a flamegraph: lots of time in `serialize_event` and `json.dumps` per tool-arg. seems like we added an extra encode step and a flush timer.
liam: reproducer: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://canary.internal/v1/chat/stream` — watch the first SSE chunk arrive ~200ms later than before.
sana: any config flags? maybe someone changed the SSE flush interval?
morgan: config diff from the PR:
```
# before PR
sse_flush_interval_ms = 0
# after PR
sse_flush_interval_ms = 20
# also: serializer now accumulates frames until newline and then flushes
```
arjun: git bisect result (snippet):
```
$ git bisect start
bad 9b7c4f2
good f3a8b2d
9b7c4f2 is first bad commit
commit 9b7c4f2
Author: tess <tess@redwood.company>
Message: rework/protocol: unify frame serialization and add buffered flush
```
jaz: that matches my tracing — buffered flush + per-tool json.dumps = extra serialization + timer = latency spike on streaming/tool calls.
morgan: opened revert PR #2352 to revert the buffered flush and the extra encode. marking as rollout-blocker for canary and dedicated.
sana: can we cherry-pick only the other fixes from 9b7c4f2 and keep them? might be worth extracting the non-stream bits.
liam: agreed. we'll revert as hotfix, then re-landing a smaller patch that preserves correctness but doesn't introduce timer-based buffering.
deploy-bot: revert PR #2352 merged to main; canary redeploy queued (pipeline: eng-ci).
eng-ci-bot: perf-check job started (synthetic-streaming) against sha revert-2352.
arjun: after revert, running the same curl repro locally — first SSE chunk timing back to baseline (~40ms). p99 dropped from 820ms to ~230ms in our local synthetic test.
jaz: monitoring canary metrics now, initial signs are good. I'll keep an eye on tool-call paths for any hidden regression.
morgan: follow-up: filing issue PERF-1187 to redesign streaming serialization: goals = avoid per-token json.dumps, remove timer-based flush, add microbench and unit perf test for SSE boundary timing. assign to arjun + tess.
sana: thanks everyone — good triage speed. once the hotfix is stable we'll unblock rollouts. :thumbsup:
liam: note for postmortem: add coverage for canary perf checks when protocol changes touch serialization or streaming layers.
arjun: adding a small benchmark to eng-runtime CI to catch similar p99 regressions before merge.
morgan: closing thread for now, will update PERF-1187 with reproducer and bisect outputs.
